title: No impact on INDIA alliance prospects in view of AIMIM-ASP pact, says Congress-SP
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
The Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Congress on Friday (November 13, 2026) said the alliance of All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) will have no impact on voters from social groups facing injustice under the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Uttar Pradesh. They added voters are aware that only INDIA alliance comprising of the SP-Congress is capable in defeating the BJP decisively. 

“Even before the announcement of AIMIM-ASP (KR) alliance, people were expecting that the BJP will try to divide the votes of Dalits, Muslims, backwards and progressive sections of society. But we believe people are fully aware that what is real end game of any such front. People across sections of the society are fully behind the INDIA alliance, and are waiting for assembly polls to defeat the anti-people BJP government,” said Shahnawaz Alam, National Secretary, Congress. 

The SP said Dalits and Muslims at the ground level remain cautious about the sudden, unnatural alliance. “The alliance of AIMIM and ASP (KR) has formed the Samajik Parivartan Morcha (Front for Social Change) to attract anti-incumbency votes from the BJP government, primarily among Scheduled Castes and Muslims. The Samajwadi Party welcomes any effort to expose communal forces that use false promises to attract voters, particularly Dalits. While the front might shift 2% to 3% of the vote away from the BJP—potentially benefiting the INDIA alliance—Dalits and Muslims at the ground level remain cautious about the intent and viability of this sudden, unnatural alliance. Although Dalits and Muslims are part of the Samajwadi Party’s socio-political platform (PDA), there is limited cohesion on the ground. Ultimately, this arrangement is unlikely to alter the election prospects of the INDIA alliance,” said Sudhir Panwar, a senior SP leader. 

On November 12, All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) president Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) chief Chandrashekhar Azad announced a political alliance for the 2027 state Assembly elections, a first declared non-National Democratic Alliance (NDA), non-INDIA bloc political front in Uttar Pradesh, with both parties considered marginal players eyeing to consolidate Scheduled Caste (SC) and minority voters in the politically crucial state. The alliance, Samajik Parivartan Morcha, for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, named Mr. Azad as the candidate for Chief Minister.

title: After CBI, ED arrests Mahadev betting app scam accused
author: Shubhomoy Sikdar
content_html:
The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Friday (November 13, 2026) said it has arrested Saurabh Chandrakar, co-owner and promoter of the Mahadev Online Book illegal betting syndicate, and would now be confronting with the evidence of money laundering against him.

Earlier on Thursday (November 12, 2026), a special CBI court remanded Chandrakar to seven days’ judicial custody and dismissed ED’s application to execute their non-bailable warrant against him. On Friday (November 13, 2026) post the arrest, the ED produced him at a special PMLA [Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002] court in Raipur which remanded him to ED custody for seven days till November 19 for further investigation.

“In ED custody, Saurabh Chandrakar will be confronted with the statements of his associates, digital data and documents concerning his foreign entities and evidence of commission of offence of money laundering,” an ED official said.

According to the ED, Chandrakar and another co-promoter Ravi Uppal operated “Mahadev Online Book” (various online betting websites) from Head Office in Dubai through a franchise of “betting panels” across India and the United Arab Emirates.

A statement further noted that player money went through bank accounts held in other people’s names and left India through hawala. ED’s main complaint of October 2023 estimated the syndicate’s earnings at about ₹450 crore a month.

“Saurabh Chandrakar did not answer the summons issued to him by ED in September 2023 and continued to evade investigation by law enforcement agencies. On ED’s application, the Special Court issued a Non-Bailable Warrant against him on 04.09.2023, and shortly thereafter, INTERPOL also published a Red Notice against him on ED’s request. His challenge to the warrant was dismissed by the High Court of Chhattisgarh on 22.03.2025. He obtained a passport of Vanuatu while holding an Indian passport, and even claimed before the Special Court that he had given up Indian citizenship on 28.06.2022,” the official said.

On the progress of the investigations into money laundering allegations, the official said that the ED had thus far searched about 190 premises, seized or frozen about ₹2,000 crore and attached property now valued at about ₹3,500 crore, about ₹1,800 crore of it abroad, including 22 immovable properties in Dubai. It has filed six prosecution complaints against 116 accused. Saurabh Chandrakar is the fifteenth person arrested by ED in this case, the ED statement noted.

The agency purportedly followed the money from panel operators through the Dubai Head Office to hawala handlers and share-market investors. “It froze securities of about ₹236 crore held by Dubai companies in September 2023. In July 2026 ED arrested Vikas Garg, whose companies received about ₹940 crore of betting proceeds, of which about ₹766 crore went into the acquisition of the United States company Ebix Inc. ED has attached about ₹941 crore in that limb,” the official said.

The ED statement also mentioned Chandrakar’s lavish wedding in UAE in the year 2023. “The wedding at Ras Al Khaimah in February 2023 cost about ₹200 crore in cash, with three chartered aircraft from Nagpur. ED traced that money through the event company, hotels and angadia firms, and the guest list it recovered identified the management of the syndicate,” the official added.

title: NHRC seeks Education Ministry’s response over alleged neglect of Veer Baal Diwas in schools
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Friday sought an explanation from the Union Ministry of Education over allegations that schools across the country give greater prominence to Children’s Day celebrations on November 14 while failing to adequately highlight the historical significance of Veer Baal Diwas, observed on December 26.

The Commission’s bench, headed by member Priyank Kanoongo, acted on a complaint submitted by Sanjeev Newar of the Seva Nyay Utthan Foundation, which raised concerns about the limited awareness among school students regarding the courage and supreme sacrifice of the four Sahibzadas of Guru Gobind Singh.

The Commission hence issued a notice to the Secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, Government of India asking whether the Central Government or any competent authority has issued an official notification, order or circular declaring November 14 as Children’s Day. If such a directive exists, the Ministry has been asked to furnish a copy and provide the relevant details.

The Ministry has been directed to submit a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within 14 days, addressing the concerns raised in the complaint.

The NHRC has also sought clarification on whether schools are being encouraged to conduct dedicated educational and awareness programmes on December 26 to commemorate Veer Baal Diwas. Such initiatives, the Commission has indicated, should help students understand the historical significance of the four Sahibzadas and their extraordinary courage and sacrifice.

Highlighting the broader educational implications of the issue, the Commission stressed the need to ensure that children are exposed to important chapters of India’s history and cultural heritage. It observed that educational institutions play a significant role in nurturing awareness of values such as bravery, faith, sacrifice and resistance to injustice.

title: Vigilance Awareness Week concludes at NLCIL
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Prasanna Kumar Acharya, chairman and managing director of NLC India Limited (NLCIL) has called for greater transparency and visibility in organisational systems in NLCIL, and the elimination of manual interventions.

He was speaking at the valedictory function of the Vigilance Awareness Week 2026 in Neyveli on Thursday.

Speaking at the meeting, Mr. Acharya said that contract manuals and operational procedures were being updated to strengthen accountability and ensure seamless governance. He appreciated the Vigilance Division’s outreach and preventive initiatives organised under the Central Vigilance Commission’s (CVC) theme, ‘Probity for Prosperity’.

Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) Appakannu Govindarajan said that this year’s CVC guidelines reflected a shift from focusing on corruption to proactively promoting integrity, honesty, and probity. With NLCIL preparing for large-scale expansion, reducing procedural errors, strengthening capacity building, and keeping pace with technological advances were essential for innovation and sustained growth, a press release quoted him as having said.

Highlighting public participation in the campaign, Mr. Govindarajan said reels and rangoli competitions had attracted people from different sections of society. He also stressed the contribution of employees and students to societal development.

Director (Mines) Suresh Chandra Suman recalled Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel’s contribution to nation-building and commended the Vigilance Division for involving the public in the campaign.

A special edition of NLCIL’s in-house vigilance magazine, Neyveli Vigil, was released on the occasion.

Mr. Acharya, functional directors Samir Swarup, Rajesh Pratap Singh Sisodia, P.L.S.S. Chaitanya Prakash, and the CVO presented prizes to employees and the winners of various competitions.

title: Two-year-old dies after firecracker explodes inside his mouth
author: Shubhomoy Sikdar
content_html:
A two-year-old boy died after a firecracker exploded inside his mouth in Chhattisgarh’s Surguja district, according to his family members.

The victim Aditya’s parents told journalists that on November 9, the boy put a pop-pop firecracker — that’s called lehsun due to its garlic like shape and is designed to explode when thrown on the ground — in his mouth while playing.

His father Indrajit Manjhi said the firecracker exploded inside his mouth, injuring his gums and causing bleeding. After other children informed the parents about the mishap, the child was first taken to a community health centre in Sitapur and brought back home after the bleeding stopped. However, when the bleeding started again, he was taken back to the health centre next day. Later, he was taken to a mission hospital in Ambikapur on November 11 where he succumbed to his injuries the same night.

The police have registered an accidental death report and further investigation is underway, the father added.

title: File FIR against those who tarnish party’s image says Bengal BJP chief
author: Shiv Sahay Singh
content_html:
Observing that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power without the support of those trying to make into the party now, president of the party’s West Bengal unit Samik Bhattacharya on Friday (November 13, 2026) said that FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish the image of the party.

“Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers, I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said. The remarks made by the Bengal BJP chief have been made at a time when there are allegations that leaders and supporters of other parties are trying to join the BJP. There have been certain reports of BJP supporters allegedly indulging in extortion after the party came to power, a charge that was levelled against Trinamool Congress leaders when the party was in power. “BJP has reached here (came to power) by keeping them out. BJP has no need to touch them,” he said.

Mr. Bhattacharya said that there can be some ‘deviations’ and the “party will correct them”. The BJP leader said anyone cannot claim allegiance to the party simply by garlanding BJP leaders. “The door was closed before; it is still closed. The door has not been officially opened,” he said. The remarks by the Bengal BJP chief come amidst claims that it is facing a challenge of “Trinamoolisation of the BJP” and Mr. Bhattacharya has been saying that the party will resist it.

BJP leaders to be appointed ward coordinators

While the BJP president warned against outsiders getting into the party, he made it clear that it will be BJP leaders who are appointed as ward commissioners. Mr. Bhattacharya said that the party will not take suggestions from Md. Salim, the CPI(M) State secretary or any other party to appoint coordinators to oversee civic services in Kolkata and Howrah if municipal elections were delayed.

“They (the ward coordinators) will be BJP people,” he said. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had said that the government will appoint coordinators in the wards of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation if the stay on civic polls is not lifted by the Supreme Court. 

The Calcutta High Court on October 6 restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.
